char1.appearance: Seraphina stands tall and proud in gleaming plate armor etched with celestial motifs. A faint radiance seems to cling to her bronze-hued skin, hinting at her otherworldly lineage. Her eyes glow with a soft golden light whenever she invokes her sacred powers, and a cascade of pale blonde hair falls from beneath her helmet. Despite a few scars from battle on her shield arm, she carries herself with graceful nobility. Every aspect of her appearance—from the meticulous care of her armor to the polished silver holy symbol around her neck—reflects discipline, piety, and noble upbringing.
char1.backstory: Born the second daughter of a venerable noble house, Seraphina’s destiny was touched by the divine from the moment of her birth. As a child she felt a strong pull toward the sacred, often wandering the family chapel and poring over tales of saints and legendary heroes. Her celestial heritage revealed itself in subtle ways — a warm glow to her healing touch, a comforting light that surrounded her during prayer. Rather than remain in courtly luxury, Seraphina chose to join the holy Knights of the Radiant Sword as soon as she came of age. Through years of rigorous training, she tempered her compassion with discipline and learned the arts of war. Her mettle was tested when an undead horde, unleashed by a corrupt necromancer, threatened her family’s lands. Seraphina rallied villagers and knights alike, standing at the forefront shining with divine conviction. They prevailed, but not before she watched her beloved mentor fall in battle to protect her. From that day, Seraphina redoubled her vows to uphold the light. She now wanders the realm as a beacon of hope—mediating disputes, defending the innocent, and challenging any darkness that arises. Though confident in her cause, she carries the memory of her mentor’s sacrifice as both a source of strength and a reminder of the cost of duty. Her life is one of service and unwavering honor, as she strives to fulfill both the expectations of her noble family and the higher calling of her celestial guides.
char1.bonds: She is devoted to the Knights of the Radiant Sword, the holy order that trained her, and considers each of her fellow paladins as family. Seraphina is also bound by duty to her ancestral lands and the common folk living there; their safety and prosperity are her personal responsibility. Her blessed longsword—once wielded by her fallen mentor—remains at her side as a constant reminder of the sacrifice that inspires her to be better.
char1.flaws: Seraphina’s trusting nature can verge on naivety; she sometimes takes people at their word if they speak of noble intentions, which leaves her open to manipulation. Her strict moral code can make her judgmental or inflexible when others offer more pragmatic solutions that bend the rules. She also shoulders blame heavily—if ever an innocent suffers under her watch, she internalizes the failure and struggles with guilt and self-doubt.
char1.ideals: Justice and Compassion—Seraphina believes the strong have a sacred duty to protect the weak, and that true justice must be tempered with mercy. She holds honesty and honor as fundamental, convinced that righteousness must never be compromised even in the face of great temptation.
char1.name: Seraphina
char1.personalityTraits: Warm, gracious, and earnest, Seraphina treats even common strangers with the courtesy of a courtly lady. She has a naturally uplifting presence and often encourages others with sincere, inspiring words. In leadership roles she is courageous and decisive—always first to charge into danger and last to retreat. When confronted by cruelty or injustice, her gentle demeanor hardens into steely determination, and she can be fearlessly uncompromising. In quieter moments, Seraphina is reflective and devout, frequently found in prayer or polishing her armor. She listens well to others’ concerns and offers guidance or comfort freely, embodying the ideals of the compassionate knight.

char2.appearance: Marcus is a broad-shouldered, weather-worn man whose stance and bearing immediately mark him as a career soldier. He keeps his half-plate armor clean and serviceable, with a faded regimental insignia etched onto one shoulder plate. His face is rugged and stern: a deep scar cuts across his left cheek, and his dark brown hair is cropped short in military fashion. Steely gray eyes constantly scan his surroundings, ever vigilant for threats. He wears a longbow and quiver strapped across his back, and a plain longsword at his hip, all arranged for easy reach. Everything about Marcus’s appearance is utilitarian and efficient—from the pragmatic way he packs his gear to the no-frills earth-toned cloak draped over his shoulders. Even at rest, he carries himself with the alert poise of someone who expects trouble and is prepared to meet it.
char2.backstory: Marcus was born to a poor cobbler and his wife in a small village, but found his true calling when he enlisted in the royal army as a young man. Military life shaped him: through long marches, endless drills, and the unforgiving reality of war, he became a disciplined and steady soldier. Marcus served in the Archer Corps of King Aldric’s army for many years, defending the kingdom’s frontiers against orc raiders and bandit incursions. He earned a reputation for level-headed leadership under fire, eventually rising to the rank of sergeant. In a infamous battle at Redfield Bridge, Marcus’s company was ambushed and nearly overwhelmed—he coordinated a defensive line with such composure that the enemy advance was stalled until reinforcements arrived. For his bravery and tactics, he received a Medal of Valor from the king’s own hand. But the victory came at a high cost: many of Marcus’s closest comrades fell that day. After the war quieted, Marcus struggled to adapt to a peaceful garrison life haunted by memories of those lost. With honorably discharge papers in hand, he decided to take his skills on the road. Now he works as a freelance guardsman and scout, lending his bow to those who need protection or tactical know-how. He remains steadfastly loyal to the ideals of the army—order, duty, and keeping the peace—carrying the legacy of his fallen brothers-in-arms wherever he travels.
char2.bonds: Marcus remains deeply loyal to the memory of his old unit. He keeps a list of names of the comrades he lost and visits their graves or memorials whenever possible. His former captain, now an aging knight, is like a father figure to him — Marcus would travel any distance to aid the man. He also feels responsible for the common folk of the realm he once swore to defend; when he protects a village from marauders or a caravan from bandits, he imagines he’s keeping the promise he made as a young recruit.
char2.flaws: Marcus can be inflexible, sometimes dismissing new ideas if they don’t mesh with his training or experience. Years of taking orders have made him uncomfortable with uncertainty, so he tends to default to strict plans and can struggle when improvisation is required. He also carries quiet guilt over the soldiers he couldn’t save — late at night, the memories of lost comrades weigh on him, and he finds solace in polishing his weapons or keeping watch, unable to fully relax. Emotionally, he is reserved; some see him as cold, but in truth he just doesn’t easily express softer feelings after so many years of war.
char2.ideals: Discipline and Order — Marcus lives by a simple creed: obey the law, do your duty, and everything else will follow. He believes a clear chain of command and adherence to regulations are what prevent society from descending into chaos. Even as a free agent now, he strives to conduct himself with honor and to uphold the soldierly principles drilled into him.
char2.name: Marcus
char2.personalityTraits: Stoic and pragmatic, Marcus approaches problems like a battlefield strategist. He values efficiency and dislikes unnecessary chatter or showboating. He wakes before dawn out of habit, often using the extra time to check his gear or survey the area. While he can come off as gruff or strictly business, Marcus quietly looks after those in his charge — offering a canteen to a thirsty traveler or a word of advice to a green militia member. He has a dry, subtle sense of humor that emerges on rare occasions around trusted allies, usually taking them by surprise. In conflict, he is unflappable and authoritative, barking concise commands and maintaining formation. He respects people who pull their weight and keep their word, and once someone has proven their reliability, they earn a steadfast ally in Marcus. However, he has little patience for laziness, chaos, or those who endanger others through folly.

char3.appearance: Thorgar is a hulking half-orc with corded muscles and a fearsome, feral demeanor. He eschews heavy armor, instead going bare-chested into battle with only a wolf-fur cloak draped over his scarred shoulders. Jagged white war paint slashes across his chest and face, highlighting the intense glare of his yellowed eyes. His slate-gray skin is littered with scars from countless brawls, and a broken tusk juts up from his lower lip, giving his perpetual scowl an even more menacing twist. Around his thick neck hangs a grisly trophy necklace strung with the fangs and teeth of beasts—and a few humanoids—he’s slain. Thorgar hefts a massive greataxe casually in one hand; the weapon’s chipped blade and dried bloodstains speak to its brutal history. Every movement he makes is predatory and unrestrained, like a wolf pacing on the edge of a kill.
char3.backstory: Thorgar’s life began in blood and hardship. Born on the fringes of civilization to a human mother and orc father, he never truly belonged in either world. Ridiculed and ostracized as a child in a human settlement, he learned that pain is power and that fear keeps you alive. As a youth, Thorgar fell in with a roaming band of bandits after beating a grown man senseless in a tavern brawl; the outlaws saw potential in the savage half-orc and took him under their wing. In the wilderness and outlaw camps, he finally found a place where brutality was an asset and not a mark of shame. Thorgar quickly became the band’s enforcer, relishing every caravan raid and village pillaging. During the infamous sacking of a border town called Riverbend, Thorgar earned his reputation: he personally smashed through the militia’s shield wall and cut down their captain, roaring in triumph as the town burned around him. With each victory, his taste for carnage grew. Violence became not just a means of survival but the very thing that gave his life meaning. Now a wanted man in several provinces, Thorgar doesn’t bother hiding from the bounty hunters who occasionally track him — he welcomes the challenge, viewing it as yet another fight to feed his endless appetite for mayhem. Untethered by clan or conscience, he wanders from one violent escapade to the next, carving his name into the world with every swing of his axe. The only legacy he cares to leave is a trail of fear and whispered stories about the half-orc who cannot be tamed.
char3.bonds: His true loyalty is to his own gang of raiders – the only semblance of family he’s ever known. Thorgar will fight tooth and nail for those unscrupulous companions who have shed blood alongside him (though he’d just as soon turn on them if they show weakness). He also harbors a twisted connection to his orc heritage; deep down, he yearns to prove himself the equal or superior of any full-blooded orc chieftain. The largest fang on his necklace was taken from the throat of a mighty orc warrior he challenged and slew, a trophy that symbolizes Thorgar’s determination to outdo his lineage.
char3.flaws: Thorgar is ruled by his temper and impulses, often to his detriment. He has no patience for subtlety or strategy, charging headlong into fights that a wiser individual would avoid. He lacks any semblance of patience or subtlety—if something isn’t happening fast enough, he’ll smash through and damn the consequences. His pride is colossal: he cannot back down from a challenge to his strength, no matter how dangerous, which makes it easy for cunning foes to bait him. He’s also indulgent to a fault, prone to bingeing on ale, food, or other pleasures after a victory, leaving him off-guard at times. Deep down, Thorgar is haunted by an insatiable need to prove himself, meaning he will pick fights with the biggest adversary in the room even if it might get him killed. His refusal to retreat or back down from any challenge is as much a curse as it is a point of pride.
char3.ideals: Might Makes Right — Thorgar firmly believes that strength is the only truth in this world. The weak exist to be dominated or destroyed. Laws and morals are nothing but fragile shields for those too feeble to seize what they want. He embraces chaos and conflict, trusting in raw power and ferocity to carry the day.
char3.name: Thorgar
char3.personalityTraits: Brash, brutal, and boasting, Thorgar lives life at full volume. He laughs loudly (often at others’ fear) and has a mocking, dark sense of humor. He tends to solve problems with intimidation or violence first and seldom bothers with any alternative. Boredom irritates him—he grows restless and spoiling for a fight if he’s too long without action. Thorgar is surprisingly straightforward in his wants: good drink, easy plunder, and opponents worth smashing. He respects raw strength and courage, even in enemies, but has nothing but scorn for weakness or cowardice. When enraged, he becomes almost animalistic: shouting Oaths in Orcish, baring his tusks, and showing a reckless disregard for his own safety. Outside of battle, he can be surly and uncooperative in any team setting unless he’s clearly the one in charge or sees personal gain. Trust does not come easily to him—he assumes everyone is as ruthlessly opportunistic as he is.

char4.appearance: Calina is a petite halfling with twinkling hazel eyes and a perpetual hint of a grin on her lips. Sunshine has freckled her tan skin, and a halo of curly chestnut-brown hair bounces around her cheeks when she moves. She dresses in simple, earth-toned clothes suited for travel: a linen tunic under a snug leather vest, and breeches tucked into soft boots made for quiet steps. A hooded green cloak—frayed from many adventures—often shadows her small form, making it easy for her to blend into a crowd or a hedgerow. Though modest in stature, Calina carries an air of confidence. A coiled rope hangs at her belt beside a sheathed short sword, and a quiver of arrows peeks over one shoulder, paired with a finely crafted shortbow. Her fingers are nimble and often ink-stained or smudged with flour, evidence of her twin loves of map-drawing and sneaking the occasional bakery treat. At a glance, most might take her for an innocent traveler or a farmer’s daughter, but the keen alertness in her eyes suggests there’s more to this cheerful halfling than meets the eye.
char4.backstory: Calina grew up in a humble farming village where everyone knew everyone, and life’s problems were usually solved with a helping hand from a neighbor. From a young age, she had a knack for mischief and a heart of gold in equal measure. She’d sneak extra sweets from the village baker only to hand them out to other children who had none. As she entered her teens, harder times befell her village. A cruel nobleman imposed heavy taxes that left many families destitute. Calina couldn’t stand to see her friends and neighbors suffer. Late one autumn night, she crept into the noble’s storehouse through an unlocked loft window and made off with a sack of grain and a handful of gold coins. By dawn, those supplies found their way to the hungriest families’ doorsteps. Her daring kindness continued in secret: whenever a villager fell ill or a child went missing in the woods, Calina was first to volunteer to set things right (often in disguise or under cover of darkness). Over time, her acts of quiet heroism became local legend. When bandits attempted to kidnap the innkeeper’s son, it was Calina who tracked their camp and freed the boy, tricking the drunk bandit guards with playful taunts and leading them on a wild goose chase. These exploits eventually drew unwanted attention from the nobleman and his cronies. Branded a “troublemaking thief,” Calina was forced to leave her beloved village to avoid retribution. Since then, she has wandered from town to town as a folk hero in the making, using her cunning and light fingers to help those suffering under tyranny or misfortune. Though she misses home dearly, Calina knows in her heart that her journey brings hope to many. Every time she topples a cruel merchant’s scheme or foils a corrupt official, she feels the pride of her village behind her, spurring her on to the next adventure.
char4.bonds: Her heart remains in her home village of Oakdale, and she regularly sends a portion of whatever coin she "liberates" back to the townsfolk (through trusted intermediaries) to ease their burdens. Calina is also bonded to those she’s befriended on the road: an elderly ranger who once hid her from mercenaries, the poor innkeeper’s family she saved from bandits, and countless common folk who showed her kindness. She wears a simple braided bracelet given to her by the children of her village as a constant reminder of why she fights. Anyone threatening those she calls family or friends will quickly earn Calina’s undying enmity.
char4.flaws: Calina’s daring can cross into recklessness. She often takes bold risks for the sake of others, sometimes without fully thinking through the consequences to herself. She also has a mischievous streak that can get her into trouble — she finds it hard to resist playing pranks on pompous authority figures or pilfering shiny trinkets that catch her eye, even when discretion would be wiser. Her deep compassion means she shoulders guilt for failures keenly; if she can’t save someone in need, she broods over it and might overextend herself next time to "make amends." Lastly, her trust in the good of ordinary people can border on naivety; she has been duped before by a sob story and likely will be again, preferring to risk being fooled than refuse someone who might truly need help.
char4.ideals: Charity and Freedom — Calina firmly believes that those with the ability to help have a duty to do so. No one should go hungry or live in fear under the heel of the powerful. She values fairness and kindness, thinking that a clever mind and a caring heart can undermine tyranny more effectively than brute force can.
char4.name: Calina
char4.personalityTraits: Optimistic and quick-witted, Calina greets most days with a smile and a quip at the ready. She has a natural ability to put others at ease — whether by cracking a gentle joke or offering a fresh-baked roll pulled from her pack — which makes people open up to her easily. Calina is a storyteller at heart; around the fire, she’ll regale friends with humorous (and wildly exaggerated) tales of her escapades, often casting herself as the "humble trickster" rather than the hero. In serious situations, however, she focuses with surprising intensity, her small frame radiating determination. She finds violence distasteful and will seek creative solutions first: setting clever traps, using disguises, or stirring distractions to achieve her goals. Still, if innocent lives are at stake, Calina’s warm demeanor hardens and she won’t hesitate to stand toe-to-toe with foes much larger than herself (usually armed with a clever plan or two). She’s fiercely loyal to her friends and genuinely believes that a bit of kindness and cleverness can light even the darkest hour.

char5.appearance: Kaelin is a lean half-elf man with sun-bronzed skin and an air of quiet vigilance. He moves with the fluid, purposeful grace of a wildcat, making hardly a sound as he steps. His ash-blond hair is loosely tied back, revealing slightly pointed ears and sharp, green eyes that constantly scan his surroundings. Kaelin’s attire is perfectly suited to the wilderness: he wears a hooded cloak patterned in mottled greens and browns, which helps him blend into forests and hillsides. Beneath it, his leather armor is well-worn and scarred by claw marks, clearly functional rather than decorative. Across his back he carries a longbow nearly as tall as he is, and a quiver of gray-fletched arrows fanning out above his shoulder. Twin scimitars hang sheathed at his sides, the simple hilts wrapped in hide for a sure grip. His tan travel boots and gloves are caked with a bit of dried mud and moss, and one can often catch the scent of pine needles and campfire smoke about him. Though not outwardly imposing, Kaelin’s presence is grounded and alert — the subtle confidence of one who has survived countless nights under the open sky.
char5.backstory: Kaelin was born where the edges of civilization meet the wild—his mother was an elven scout and his father a human trapper in a frontier hamlet. From the time he could walk, Kaelin was more at home under the canopy of ancient trees than behind any city walls. He learned to track deer along fern-carpeted paths, to fish the rushing streams, and to recognize the growls in the night that meant danger. In his youth, a tragedy struck: marauding gnolls attacked a nearby homestead that Kaelin frequented, leaving devastation in their wake. Kaelin narrowly saved two younger children by leading them into the dense woods to hide, but the gnolls’ massacre left an indelible mark on him. In the aftermath, a seasoned ranger from the King’s Wood took Kaelin under his wing, teaching him to channel his grief into guardianship of the wild and the innocent. Under the ranger’s mentorship, Kaelin developed into a skilled hunter of evil creatures: he learned the weak points of orcs, how to move silently against the wind, and the calls of every bird that might signal approaching danger. As an adult, Kaelin became a wanderer, patrolling the borderlands and unclaimed wilderness where few others cared to go. He guided lost travelers, drove off monsters that threatened remote farms, and negotiated peace between encroaching settlers and aggrieved fey creatures. His deeds—like slaying a rampaging owlbear or uniting feuding lumberjacks and dryads—usually go unsung except in the grateful whispers of those he’s helped. Kaelin prefers it that way. Now he lives by moving camp to camp, a solitary warden quietly ensuring that both civilization and nature can coexist in balance. Whenever he passes through a village plagued by something lurking in the dark, the townsfolk take heart—for the soft-spoken half-elf with the longbow has never once failed to see them through the night.
char5.bonds: He remains deeply grateful to the old ranger who saved him and taught him his trade; Kaelin keeps his mentor’s worn hunting knife as a token of that bond and strives to live up to the ranger’s example. He’s also attached to a small village on the forest’s edge — the place he once helped rebuild after a gnoll raid. Though he rarely stays long, he often circles back there to ensure its people are safe, silently mending fences or leaving behind game meat for them. Additionally, Kaelin holds dear a tattered field journal filled with herbal remedies and hand-drawn maps that belonged to his elven mother; protecting these last links to his family’s legacy is a promise he has made to himself.
char5.flaws: Kaelin is used to fending for himself and can be slow to trust others to handle dangerous situations. He often prefers to take on burdens alone rather than risk someone else getting hurt, which can make him seem aloof or uncooperative in a team. His long stretches in the wild have left him a bit socially awkward; he can be blunt or taciturn, and he finds the formalities of courts or large towns uncomfortable and pointless. Old pain still lurks beneath his calm surface — when faced with creatures like gnolls or others that mindlessly slaughter the defenseless, Kaelin’s controlled demeanor can crack, giving way to anger that might cloud his judgement. And while he preaches balance, there’s a part of him that struggles to find balance in his own heart, teetering between the solitary path he thinks he deserves and the companionship he secretly longs for.
char5.ideals: Balance and Guardianship — Kaelin believes that the world works best when no one force — whether human greed or nature’s fury — overtakes the other. He is devoted to protecting the innocent and preserving the natural order. To him, mercy and vigilance go hand in hand: a true guardian must sometimes be the predator that keeps worse predators at bay.
char5.name: Kaelin
char5.personalityTraits: Soft-spoken and even-tempered, Kaelin tends to observe more than he talks. He chooses his words carefully and rarely raises his voice, even when issuing warnings or commands. He is respectful to all, from the lowliest farmer to the haughtiest elf lord, but one might notice he reserves true warmth for children, animals, and those genuinely in need. Having spent so much time alone, he’s perfectly content with silence and can sit with companions for hours without any urge to fill the quiet — an attribute that some find calming and others find mysterious. Kaelin has an inherent love of nature that shows in small ways: a slight smile when he hears wolves howl in the distance, or the gentle way he handles an injured bird while treating it. In dangerous situations, he becomes focused and methodical, issuing concise directions in a calm, steady voice that can steady panicked nerves. While he isn’t the first to laugh or sing in a tavern, he shows his warmth through small gestures: a faint smile when a friend tells a joke, or a reassuring hand on the shoulder of a frightened villager. The longer one travels with Kaelin, the more they notice his subtle appreciation for life’s simple pleasures—a sunrise through the trees, the camaraderie of a shared campfire meal, or the soft hoot of an owl at night. Those are the moments that anchor him and remind him why he wanders so far to keep the balance.

char6.appearance: Zevnir cuts an imposing figure, tall and gaunt with the regal bearing of a noble and the unnerving aura of one who traffics in dark powers. As a drow, his skin is the color of polished obsidian, and it contrasts sharply with his long, silvery-white hair that falls past his shoulders in neat, silken strands. His eyes gleam a vivid crimson, often alight with a calculating, cruel intelligence. He is clad in flowing robes of the deepest midnight black, trimmed with arcane sigils embroidered in silver thread. The robes themselves seem to drink in the light; small wisps of shadow cling to the fabric as if obeying his unspoken command. In one slender hand Zevnir carries an ebon staff topped with a wrought-iron claw clutching a dark crystal orb. Occasionally, flickers of eerie green witch-light crackle within the orb when his mood sours or his magic surges. Around his neck hangs a fine silver chain with a single onyx pendant, and ornate rings adorn several fingers — each inset with gemstones that glint with an inner fire. Despite the finery, there’s a cold austerity to him: his movements are precise and measured, every aspect of his attire immaculate and deliberate. When Zevnir fixes someone with his gaze, it feels as if a predator is examining prey — detached, confident, and utterly without fear.
char6.backstory: Zevnir was born into a minor noble house in the subterranean drow city of Xil’vraen, Zevnir learned early that knowledge is power—and in the cutthroat society of the drow, power was the only means to survive. As a male in a matriarchal world, he was denied the priesthood of Lolth, but he discovered a different path to influence: the arcane. He apprenticed under the city’s aging Archmage, where his keen intellect and cold determination quickly became apparent. Zevnir poured over forbidden tomes by the light of bioluminescent fungi, mastering spells that few dared to attempt. In secret, he also began experimenting with necromancy, finding a grim fascination in bending life and death to his will. When a coup within his house threatened to eliminate him (along with any other inconvenient heirs), Zevnir struck first. In one night of terror, shadowy figures and reanimated horrors loyal to Zevnir wiped out the rival nobles. By dawn, House Xil’vraen lay in ruin and Zevnir had vanished into the tunnels of the Underdark with his grim grimoire and ambitions intact. In the centuries that followed, Zevnir wandered in exile, constantly expanding his magical might. On the surface world, he adopted the guise of a scholarly recluse, establishing a lair in an abandoned tower far from prying eyes. Villagers in neighboring lands learned to avoid that crumbling spire—strange lights flickered at its windows on new moons, and those who wandered too close sometimes disappeared, only to return as mindless undead under his control. Zevnir delved into ancient catacombs for lost scrolls, bargained with fiends for dark knowledge, and even conversed with a lich or two in his unending quest to unlock every arcane secret. Over time, he built a network of influence: corrupt officials secretly on his payroll, necromantic cults that worshipped him as an oracle, and undead spies carrying whispers from distant cities. Now, at the pinnacle of his mortal power, Zevnir stands on the precipice of what he views as true transcendence—perhaps lichdom, or a ritual that could elevate him to a godlike state. He has long since shed any scruples or attachments that might slow his ascent. To him, ordinary lives are but candles to be snuffed out or reignited in service of his experiments. And in his meticulously crafted plans, the era of Zevnir’s reign—silent, eternal, and absolute—draws ever closer.
char6.bonds: Zevnir’s only true loyalty is to his own accumulation of arcane secrets. His spellbook—an ever-growing compendium of dark rituals and personal annotations—is arguably his closest companion, and he has safeguarded it with deadly enchantments and decades of his life. There is also a faint sentimental thread buried deep: an ancient tome given to him by his long-dead Archmage mentor. Though Zevnir surpassed (and ultimately betrayed) his teacher, he still keeps that first spellbook as a reminder of where his journey began. It is perhaps the only object that he would risk much to recover if lost. Apart from that, the necromancer’s “bonds” manifest in a possessive way: he considers the legions of undead under his command and the hidden library of scrolls in his tower as extensions of himself, jealously guarding them from any who might try to steal or destroy what is his.
char6.flaws: Zevnir’s greatest flaw is his towering arrogance. He regards most other beings—especially non-magical folk—as insignificant insects to be used or swatted away as he pleases. This overconfidence can blind him to the potential of those he underestimates. Additionally, his pursuit of immortality has made him obsessively paranoid about threats to his existence; he has layered his life with so many contingencies, wards, and backup plans that he sometimes distrusts his own allies and undermines partnerships with constant suspicion. Zevnir is also utterly uncompromising: if he sets his mind on a piece of knowledge or an artifact, he will destroy friendships, towns, or even destabilize entire regions without a second thought, which can inadvertently rally great opposition against him. Lastly, life in shadows has left him with certain drow quirks—bright sunlight physically pains and weakens him, which he detests, and it feeds a deep-seated resentment for the surface world that he must carefully manage whenever he’s forced into daylight.
char6.ideals: Absolute Knowledge — To Zevnir, knowledge is power, and power justifies all. He holds that moral restraints are the shackles of lesser minds; true wisdom lies in grasping the universe’s secrets by any means necessary. He seeks enlightenment unbound by petty concepts of good or evil. In his philosophy, those with the will to seize power have every right to dominate those who do not. Ultimately, he strives to know and control all that he can, bending the natural order to his will.
char6.name: Zevnir
char6.personalityTraits: Coldly intelligent and calculating, Zevnir is a man of few but carefully chosen words. He often speaks in a smooth, patient tone that nonetheless carries an implicit threat. He enjoys intellectual sparring and will toy with those who engage him in matters of knowledge, but his courtesy is a thin veneer over palpable condescension. Zevnir rarely shows anger overtly; when frustrated or defied, he tends to grow unnervingly still and quiet, his eyes burning with contempt while he formulates an exquisitely cruel response. He has a meticulous mind—obsessed with planning and foreseeing outcomes—and takes genuine pleasure in outmaneuvering opponents like pieces on a chessboard. Despite his disdain for most social interaction, he can adopt a facade of politeness or even charm if a situation absolutely demands it (for instance, dealing with a rival archmage or bargaining with a demon lord). In solitude or among his undead thralls, Zevnir drops all pretense: he mutters arcane equations to himself, obsessively annotates scrolls, and wanders his dark halls with an intensity that borders on madness. To those beneath his notice, he is dismissive at best. But to those rare few he considers interesting or useful, he can be surprisingly generous with his vast knowledge—at least until they cease to be of value. Above all, Zevnir carries himself with the unwavering confidence of someone who has never encountered a problem his magic couldn’t eventually solve, and that haughty self-assurance radiates from his every gesture and decision.

char7.appearance: Lilith is a vision of dark elegance. A tiefling of striking beauty, she has deep crimson skin that contrasts with the opulent, pearl-colored silks and velvets she often wears when assuming the role of a noblewoman. Her horns sweep back gracefully from her temples, polished and adorned with delicate golden caps that twinkle when they catch the light. Thick midnight-black hair falls in lustrous waves to the middle of her back, usually coiled into an immaculate updo or left cascading in a way that frames her sharp jawline. Lilith’s eyes are a molten amber, their feline shape giving her gaze an alluring, predatory quality; they glow faintly whenever she invokes her magic or her temper flares. She has refined features and a disarming smile that can transition from sweet innocence to sly knowingness in a heartbeat. Although her attire can change on a whim (thanks to subtle illusion magic woven into her glamour), she favors clothes that exude wealth and taste — corseted gowns with lace trim, high-collared jackets embroidered with infernal motifs, or on more "practical" days, well-tailored leather armor disguised as fashionable riding attire. Around her neck glints a pendant of black onyx set in an intricate gold filigree (a protective charm from her patron, though she’ll claim it’s a family heirloom). A keen observer might notice the small details that hint at her fiendish nature: the occasional swish of a pointed tail beneath her skirts or the subtle fang-like canines that show when she grins. Every aspect of Lilith’s appearance is carefully curated, whether to beguile, intimidate, or vanish into a crowd at a moment’s notice.
char7.backstory: Lilith’s early life was spent on the streets and docks of a sprawling port city, where being a tiefling meant enduring fear and superstition from the ignorant. Orphaned at a young age (or so she tells people, though the truth of her parentage is a story she’s never shared), she survived using the two tools that never failed her: a quick mind and an even quicker tongue. As a child, she learned to read human nature the way others read books — figuring out exactly what someone wanted or needed to hear, and then becoming that sweet whisper in their ear. Her natural charm and subtle magic allowed her to graduate from simple pickpocketing to elaborate confidence schemes before she was out of her teens. In one of her earliest big cons, she impersonated the lost niece of a minor lord, forging documents and easing into the role so convincingly that she nearly made off with a small fortune in jewels before an overly curious magistrate grew suspicious. Cornered and facing imprisonment, Lilith made a desperate choice that changed her fate forever. Whispering an incantation from a forbidden pamphlet she’d lifted off a cultist weeks before, she called out to any power that would listen. To her surprise, something answered. A smooth, infernal voice offered her a pact: power and escape, in exchange for her service. In that moment, Lilith agreed. The guards found only an empty shrine and a faint whiff of brimstone. From then on, Lilith’s natural cunning was augmented with eldritch magic granted by her unseen patron—a diabolic archfiend from the Hells. She honed her craft as a warlock in tandem with her skills as a con artist, using minor illusions and beguiling enchantments to elevate her schemes to an entirely new level. Under various aliases, she wormed her way into noble courts and wealthy guilds in multiple cities, charming those in power while clandestinely furthering her infernal benefactor’s agendas (which conveniently often aligned with her own pursuit of wealth and influence). Over the years, Lilith became the architect of several scandals: a mysteriously ousted baron whose secrets she blackmailed out of him under the guise of a confidante, and a merchant feud she orchestrated that ended with her quietly seizing a substantial cut of both businesses. Though few know her true identity, the criminal underworld whispers of the “Velvet Shadow,” a master manipulator and sorceress whose honeyed lies are as dangerous as any blade. Now, Lilith walks a razor’s edge—juggling her personal ambitions with the terms of her infernal contract. Every spell she casts and soul she sways feeds the pact she made, while she herself remains ever alert for an opportunity to twist free of the devil’s claw when the time is right. In the meantime, she continues to play the long con, one elegantly deceptive step at a time.
char7.bonds: By the terms of her infernal pact, Lilith is bound to serve the interests of her unseen patron — a bond written in the very blood of her soul. While not affectionate, it is a tether she cannot easily cut, and fulfilling (or cleverly subverting) her patron’s demands is a constant in her life. On a more mortal level, she holds a soft spot for her younger half-brother, a tiefling boy who still lives in the squalid district where she grew up and whom she secretly watches over from afar. Though she hasn’t spoken to him in years (he believes she died or left for good), she funnels money his way under anonymous guises and has quietly thwarted a thug’s attempt to extort him. Additionally, Lilith harbors a special fondness for one of her false identities—Lady Seraphine, a kindhearted noble persona she crafted so convincingly that even she sometimes slips into the comfort of that role’s make-believe gentility when alone. It’s a small escape from the web of lies she weaves and perhaps a glimpse of who she might have been under different stars.
char7.flaws: Lilith’s confidence in her own cleverness can border on hubris. She often underestimates how quickly a carefully spun web can unravel, especially when unpredictable emotions or heroes get involved. She is inherently distrustful—assuming everyone is running a game of their own—so she struggles to form genuine friendships or accept help, even when she desperately needs it. There’s also a cold streak in her: having spent much of her life deceiving others, she finds it difficult to be sincere even at moments when honesty would serve her better. Deep down, Lilith is secretly terrified of the eventual cost of her infernal bargain; nightmares of being dragged to the Nine Hells upon death plague her more often than she’d admit. This fear sometimes drives her to rash action, such as silencing a potential threat or betraying an ally, to protect the carefully constructed house of cards that is her life.
char7.ideals: Ambition and Cunning — Life, to Lilith, is a high-stakes game of deception and strategy. She values outsmarting and outmaneuvering others above brute strength or honest labor. Deals and promises (especially those sealed in blood) are to be honored to the letter, if not the spirit—after all, words can be bent advantageously. Ultimately, she strives for a life of comfort, influence, and security where she is beholden to no one and nothing, even if it means bending oaths or betraying allies once they’ve outlived their usefulness.
char7.name: Lilith
char7.personalityTraits: Charming, resourceful, and quick-witted, Lilith can seamlessly adapt her demeanor to her audience. In a crowded tavern, she’s the vivacious storyteller buying the next round; in a ducal court, she’s demure and graceful, every inch the well-bred lady. She has a talent for making people feel uniquely seen and understood —villagers find themselves trusting this pint-sized stranger with the infectious laugh without quite knowing why. Lilith tends to approach challenges with creativity and optimism, preferring to think her way out of a tight spot (or sneak out of it) rather than resort to violence. She’s fiercely protective of underdogs and children, and won’t hesitate to stand up to bullies many times her size (usually by outsmarting them). While she generally keeps a positive outlook, Lilith can be serious when the situation demands it; her hazel eyes harden and her small voice takes on surprising authority when she witnesses cruelty. She has a bit of a habit of snacking when she’s planning—nibbling an apple or pastry as she plots the next move. Those who get to know her see that beneath the lighthearted banter and daring stunts lies a genuinely kind soul who finds true joy in making life a little fairer for the ordinary folk around her.

char8.appearance: Balasar is a dragonborn with scales of brilliant sapphire blue, so lustrous that they seem almost metallic under bright light. He is tall and broad-shouldered, built with the imposing physique common to his kind, yet he moves with a showman’s flourish. Ridges of ivory horns crown the back of his head in a swept-back pattern, and he has a habit of polishing them to a sheen. Balasar’s eyes are a striking electric blue that crackle with energy whenever he’s excited — which is often, given his flair for drama. Unlike many of his kin who favor martial garb, Balasar dresses the part of an entertainer. On stage (and quite frequently off it), he dons a flowing crimson greatcoat with gold embroidery that catches the eye, paired with a billowy white silk shirt and tall boots that thump rhythmically when he dances or marches. A variety of colorful sashes and belts wrap around his waist, some holding pouches of trick props and others simply adding theatrical flair. He wears a short cape that he often whips off with a grand gesture when bowing to a crowd. Balasar’s claws are painted — yes, painted — in alternating colors (today might be gold and red, tomorrow perhaps green and silver) as an extra touch of flamboyance. Whether breathing a small puff of lightning into the air to punctuate a point or juggling daggers with tail and hands in a tavern, Balasar’s presence is impossible to ignore; he looks every inch the charismatic ringleader of his own one-man circus.
char8.backstory: Balasar’s earliest memories are filled with the clash of steel and the bark of drill sergeants. Hatched into a proud dragonborn clan known for its military service, he was groomed from a young age to be a warrior. But while other hatchlings reveled in combat training, Balasar found himself more enchanted by the camp bards and storytellers who spun epic tales by the evening fire. He discovered an innate magical talent when, as a child, he sneezed and accidentally released a crackle of lightning that set the tent poles humming. This sorcery, tied to his draconic blood, fascinated him—he saw it not just as a weapon, but as something wondrous. By adolescence, Balasar had earned as many reprimands for staging impromptu 'battle reenactments' (complete with illusory dragon illusions) as he had earned praise for actual sparring. His family’s frustrations grew at his lack of seriousness; Balasar was a square peg in the round hole of their martial traditions. The turning point came when a traveling carnival passed near his garrison. Sneaking out to witness it, Balasar was mesmerized by the fire-breathers, acrobats, and magicians. Here was the thrill and awe he’d been craving—without the rigid discipline that stifled him. That night, with little more than a pack of clothes and his grandmother’s lute strapped to his back, Balasar left the barracks behind and ran away to join the carnival. Life under the big top was everything he hoped: unpredictable, joyous, and full of applause. Starting off mucking stables and setting up tents, he spent every spare moment learning the performers’ crafts. A kindly illusionist taught him to weave minor spells into visual delights, and the troupe’s storyteller helped him turn his life experiences into captivating tales. Before long, 'Balasar the Stormsong' became one of the star acts—a dragonborn sorcerer who could belch lightning on cue, juggle orbs of electricity, and belt out thunderous ballads of heroism and humor. Wandering from town to town with the carnival, he honed both his magical prowess and his showmanship. The same innate magic that might have made him a formidable battlemage instead became the source of wondrous entertainment. He learned to cast spells with a flick of the wrist and a cheeky grin, often blending sleight-of-hand with true sorcery to leave audiences guessing what was trick and what was real. But life as a performer isn’t all applause and encores. Balasar’s adventures on the road have embroiled him in everything from barroom brawls (triggered by a 'harmless' joke at a thug’s expense) to daring rescues (he once used his lightning to simulate St. Elmo’s fire and scare off bandits harassing his troupe). Each escapade simply adds more material for his performances. Now a free agent, Balasar travels as a one-dragonborn show, or sometimes alongside adventuring parties when he craves real danger to spice up his performances. His journey is guided by cheers and footlights as much as by any destiny; after all, to Balasar, the world is a grand stage, and he fully intends to give it the performance of a lifetime.
char8.bonds: He remains fondly bonded to the carnival troupe that became his second family. The memory of those early days under the striped tents—when an eclectic mix of misfits and artists gave a wayward dragonborn a home—stays close to his heart. If any of them ever needed him, Balasar would rush to their aid without a second thought (and likely turn the reunion into a special performance event too). Additionally, he is fiercely protective of his audience, especially the wide-eyed children who remind him of himself when he first fell in love with showmanship. On more than one occasion, he has quietly slipped some of his earnings to a struggling local theater or an aspiring young performer in a town he’s passing through. Lastly, he carries one tangible token of his past: an old leather-bound journal full of scribbled show ideas, snippets of songs, and sketches of fantastical costumes. Tucked in the back are a few letters from his family — including one from his stern father expressing pride in Balasar’s accomplishments in his own unconventional path, a letter he keeps folded at the back of the journal as quiet validation.
char8.flaws: Balasar’s love for attention can sometimes border on narcissism. He tends to underestimate dangers, treating serious situations as if they were part of one of his performances — a mindset that has landed him (and companions) in hot water when he fails to plan properly or takes risks for the sake of flair. He’s also prone to indulge in the pleasures of the road: good ale, good praise, and good company, occasionally to excess. This devil-may-care attitude means he can be unreliable with things like keeping schedules or promises that constrain his freedom; he doesn’t mean harm, but he might skip out on a dull responsibility if a more exciting opportunity beckons. Furthermore, Balasar’s pride in his sorcerous talent makes him a bit dismissive of more "mundane" skills — he might scoff at an overly tactical plan or at caution advised by non-magical peers, preferring to wing it with style. Lastly, beneath the bravado, there’s a tiny fear that if the cheering ever stops, he’ll lose his sense of purpose. It’s not something he’d readily admit, but it drives him to constantly seek that next applause, sometimes at the expense of caution.
char8.ideals: Freedom and Expression — Balasar lives by the principle that life is meant to be lived out loud and on one’s own terms. He abhors rigid rules or anything that stifles creativity and fun. Bringing joy (or at least excitement) to others is, in his view, one of the highest callings. He believes everyone deserves a chance to step into the spotlight and be the hero of their own story, and woe to anyone who tries to curtain his performance or cage his free spirit.
char8.name: Balasar
char8.personalityTraits: Exuberant, friendly, and a bit theatrical in everything he does, Balasar tends to make an immediate impression. He laughs easily and loudly, and he’s the first to break out into a bawdy song or initiate a group toast at a tavern. He treats each day as a performance waiting to happen; even mundane tasks might prompt him to hum a tune or perform an unnecessary (but fun) flourish. Though outwardly confident and composed, he always keeps one eye on the exits and one hand near a hidden dagger or a spell ready, a testament to his underlying paranoia. Balasar can also be a bit fussy—in a lovable way—fretting over his companions’ well-being (making sure the warrior’s armor is properly buckled, or that the wizard has eaten breakfast). When tensions run high, he’s the first to mediate, using calm reasoning or a firm, gentle scolding to remind everyone of what’s important. He holds his faith deeply but wears it humbly; rather than preach, he leads by example, embodying the virtues she cherishes. One might occasionally catch her whispering a little prayer of thanks during a sunrise or gently touching a wildflower’s petals with awe—small expressions of her reverence for life’s everyday miracles.

char9.appearance: Helja is a stout dwarf woman with a welcoming, earthy presence. Her honey-brown hair is plaited into a thick braid that falls over one shoulder, intertwined with simple white ribbons – a sign of her devotion to the healing arts. She has kind, round features; laugh lines crease the corners of her amber eyes, and her cheeks are often flushed rosy (be it from exertion in battle or the warmth of a hearth). Helja wears a set of well-made chain mail under a pristine white tabard emblazoned with the golden gauntlet-and-candle symbol of her life-giving deity. Around her broad waist is cinched a leather belt from which hang healing pouches bulging with herbs, poultices, and a well-thumbed prayer book. A steel warhammer, simple in design but meticulously cared for, rests within easy reach on her belt, opposite a round wooden shield painted with a faded emblem of a rising sun. Despite the martial gear, Helja exudes a nurturing aura: she smells faintly of clean soap, herbal tonics, and fresh bread. She moves with purpose—planting each step firmly—yet there’s a softness in her gestures when she’s tending to the injured or offering a hand on a friend’s shoulder. A small holy symbol of her faith, a silver pair of interlocking rings, hangs around her neck and often catches the light as she bends over someone in prayer or care.
char9.backstory: Helja was born into a close-knit dwarven community under the mountains, where being a tiefling meant enduring fear and superstition from the ignorant. From an early age, Helja’s path diverged toward the temple of Moradin’s wife, Berronar Truesilver, patron of safety and home. From her teenage years, she apprenticed under the clan’s elder healer—a cranky but big-hearted priest—learning everything from setting broken bones to reciting ancient prayers of mending. Helja had a natural gift: a gentle bedside manner that could soothe the most agitated patient and a singing voice that, while plain, carried calming reverence during hymns. When a devastating cave-in struck the mines, young Helja worked tirelessly alongside her mentor, saving many who might have succumbed to injuries. That event affirmed her calling beyond any doubt. She took her oaths as a cleric of life and community soon after, devoting herself to being a beacon for her people. For years, Helja served in her mountain hold—delivering babies, organizing winter food drives for hungry families, and quietly performing miracles of healing when sickness swept through. But the wider world called to her in the form of travelers bearing tales of wars, plagues, and strife beyond the mountain. She realized that her capacity to help needn’t be confined to her kin alone. When a human caravan arrived with refugees wounded by an orc raid in the lowlands, Helja’s heart compelled her to action. With her clan’s blessing (and a tearful farewell from her aging mentor), she packed her healing kits, shouldered her hammer and shield, and journeyed down with the refugees to lend aid. In the years that followed, Helja wandered from village to village and battlefield to battlefield, wherever the need was greatest. She mended arms and hearts in a coastal town beset by fever, negotiated peace between rival farm families in a fertile valley, and even stood against undead horrors that blighted an old cemetery, her holy prayers burning them away to protect the living. Each spring, she makes a point to return to her mountain home to share stories and recharge her spirit among family—her letters home have become local legend, read aloud at hearths with pride. Helja’s journey has made her something of a folk heroine in the region: the kindly dwarf matron who arrives when all hope seems lost, binding wounds and restoring light. With every life saved and every community rebuilt, Helja reaffirms her belief that all creatures are one large family under the gods, and she is determined to spend the rest of her days seeing that family safe and cared for.
char9.bonds: She is deeply devoted to the temple and teachings that shaped her; the memory of her old mentor and the sacred oaths she took to uphold the ideals of home and healing are ever-present in her mind. Helja also maintains strong ties to her hometown of Karag-Dûm and the family she left behind—the memory of evenings spent around her clan’s long oak table, sharing food and laughter, fuels her desire to spread that sense of belonging wherever she goes. Additionally, Helja has formed bonds with many of those she’s healed or traveled with. She keeps a carefully folded bundle of thank-you notes and childish crayon drawings gifted to her by people she’s nursed back to health. These tokens remind her, in the toughest times, of why she must continue her work—because there are real faces and stories behind every life she saves.
char9.flaws: Helja’s compassionate nature, while a virtue, can also blind her to harsh realities. She often struggles to accept that not everyone can be saved or redeemed; this sometimes leads her to put herself (and occasionally her companions) in danger trying to reach someone entrenched in darkness. Her unwavering devotion to doing good can manifest as stubbornness—once she sets her mind on the 'right thing,' she is loath to compromise, even if a more pragmatic (but less idealistic) solution is available. Helja also tends to shoulder too much responsibility; if someone under her care is hurt or lost, she’ll quietly berate herself for failing them, carrying guilt long after others have moved on. She has the typically dwarven hard-headedness as well: when it comes to matters of safety or health, she can be downright bossy, insisting that allies rest when they want to push on, or refusing to leave behind someone injured even when strategy might demand retreat. And though she rarely shows anger, threats to the innocent or desecrations of sacred things can make her temper smolder—at times like those, her forgiveness has limits, and she must check her urge to mete out harsh justice in the heat of the moment.
char9.ideals: Compassion and Community — Helja believes that mercy, kindness, and cooperation are the highest virtues. Every life is precious, and every soul—no matter how lost—deserves comfort and a chance at redemption. She strives to be the steady flame in the dark, promoting unity among disparate folk much as dwarves gather around a warm hearth. Her moral compass is guided by the tenet that helping others isn’t just a duty, it’s the very reason the strong are given strength.
char9.name: Helja
char9.personalityTraits: Motherly in spirit and steadfast in morals, Helja often acts as the emotional anchor of any group. She is the first to wake and prepare a hearty breakfast (with strong dwarf coffee, of course) and the last to turn in after ensuring everyone’s wounds are tended and worries heard. She speaks with a gentle, reassuring tone that can firm up into a drill sergeant’s bark when someone refuses to take needed medicine or tries to wander off mid-recovery. Orderly and practical, Helja likes to keep her surroundings and travel routines tidy—she’ll hum a low dwarven lullaby while neatly bandaging injuries or polishing her armor, treating even those tasks as a form of meditation. She has a well of patience that seems bottomless: whether enduring a brash warrior’s complaints or a frightened child’s cries, she remains calm and attentive, giving solace and counsel without judgment. But pity the fool who harms a defenseless creature or mocks her patients—Helja’s stare alone, stern as granite, can make the hardest mercenary shuffle their feet like a scolded schoolboy. Despite her seriousness in duty, she has a warm laugh and enjoys simple pleasures: good stew, a rousing chorus to a tavern song (she’ll clap along even if her singing voice is modest at best), and the camaraderie of friends. Helja prays each morning and night, not in a showy way, but as one might quietly write a letter to a dear friend. Those close to her feel genuinely cared for, often referring to her affectionately as "Auntie" or "Mother" on long journeys. And indeed, Helja will fuss and fret in that manner—pressing extra food on the hungry, tugging a blanket up on the cold, and always insisting that hope remains even in dire straits. Her steadfast optimism and nurturing spirit make her a beacon of comfort, whether in the heat of battle or the quiet of a sickroom.

char10.appearance: Nissa is a diminutive forest gnome with big, curious hazel eyes and a button nose dusted with freckles. Her wavy hair, a mix of chestnut brown and mossy green strands, cascades untamed to her shoulders, often adorned with whatever nature offers that day—a sprig of holly, a few wildflowers, or a feather that got tangled during her latest animal encounter. Her skin has a warm, nutty complexion and is often smudged with a bit of dirt or pollen from her wanderings. Nissa’s clothing is a collection of practical forest garb: a tunic and trousers stitched from earthy green and brown fabrics, reinforced with patches of animal hide. Over that she wears a cloak woven from broad leaves and soft bark fibers that miraculously never seem to wilt, draping around her like a piece of living foliage. Around her neck hangs a simple pendant—a polished acorn cap on a leather cord—an old keepsake from her grove. Nissa moves with a spry energy; you might catch sight of her perched in the crook of a tree branch one moment and then see her crouched low to greet a hedgehog the next. A small brown field mouse often rides in her pockets or on her shoulder, chittering softly (one of her many animal friends that accompany her). Nissa’s presence is often heralded by the scent of pine, damp earth, and wildflowers, and sometimes even tiny mushrooms sprout in her footprints if she lingers too long in one spot.
char10.backstory: Nissa was born at the base of an ancient oak deep in the Whispering Wilds, delivered under a full moon’s light with only the forest spirits as witnesses. Her earliest playmates were squirrels and her crib a bed of soft moss. Growing up in a secluded gnome hamlet hidden from the outside world, she learned the language of chittering birds and babbling brooks before the common tongue of men. As a little girl, she would wander off for days at a time, happily conversing with sparrows or napping curled up beside a mother fox and her kits. Her 'wild streak' prompted a village elder—an old druid of the Circle of the Moon—to take her under his wing. Under his patient tutelage, Nissa learned the druidic arts: how to listen to the heartbeat of the world and channel the wild’s magic. For decades, Nissa lived simply and contentedly in that grove, tending to wounded creatures, studying the stars’ patterns through the leafy canopy, and perfecting the art of shapeshifting into the very animals she adored. Though solitary, she never felt lonely; the forest was her family and sanctuary. That tranquil life changed when a creeping blight began to poison her beloved woods. Patches of the forest turned black and brittle, and animals fell ill with no apparent cause. Desperate to save her home, Nissa ventured out to seek answers in the wider world. Her journey took her to human settlements at the forest’s edges—places she’d only heard of in distant songs. These towns bewildered her at first: so noisy and fast and disconnected from the earth. But she persisted, bartering her herbal remedies for information and offering her healing touch to earn trust. Eventually, she discovered the source of the blight: toxic runoff from an alchemist’s laboratory upstream was seeping into the soil. With a mixture of courage and naiveté, Nissa confronted the alchemist. In doing so, she befriended a band of adventurers who helped her persuade (and if need be, pressure) the alchemist to stop his careless dumping. Together, they cleansed the land through druidic ritual and hard labor. Since then, her curiosity about the wider world has blossomed. She still prefers the wilds, camping under the stars and awakening at dawn to a chorus of birds, but she no longer fears the occasional foray into a village or adventuring party to pursue a cause. Her journey outside Elderwood continues as she realizes that all lands are interconnected—what harms one forest might someday harm her own if left unchecked. Equal parts wise woman and whimsical sprite, Nissa roams wherever the wind (or a distressed animal’s call) carries her, determined to keep the natural balance and sprinkle a bit of forest magic wherever she goes.
char10.bonds: Her strongest bond is to the Whispering Wilds, her home forest. She carries a small sachet of sacred soil from under the great oak of her grove, and in lonely moments she’ll hold it and feel the comfort of home. Nissa also has a deep attachment to the animal companions she’s made over the years. She has fond memories of a wise old wolf, Greyback, who patrolled the forest with her on many a moonlit night, and a magpie named Jingle who still occasionally finds her on the road to deliver shiny trinkets or news from the Wilds. Among people, her bonds tend to form with fellow caretakers of nature or gentle souls: an elderly herbalist in one town who saved bees like they were family, or a shy ranger in another who patrolled the woods alone (she affectionately calls him her "tall two-legged brother"). These individuals, scattered though they are, have become like extended kin to her. If any sent word that they were in trouble, Nissa would travel miles without hesitation to come to their aid. Lastly, she holds dear the teachings of her old druid mentor; his tattered journal of sketches and druidic notes rides in her pack, and consulting it is like hearing his guidance whispering in her ear once more.
char10.flaws: Having spent so much time alone (and in animal form), Nissa can be awkward or blatantly honest in social situations, sometimes to the point of faux pas. She might absent-mindedly start speaking to a stranger in the singsong language of birds, or bluntly tell a pompous noble that "your aura is muddy" without realizing the offense. Her fierce love of nature can also lead to impulsive actions: she once freed a merchant’s caged exotic birds in the middle of a market without considering the consequences (some called it theft; she called it liberation). When nature is threatened or animals are harmed, Nissa’s normally sunny disposition vanishes—she can become as relentless and unpredictable as a storm. During such times she might overlook pragmatic solutions, focusing only on rectifying the wrong even if it causes other problems. Additionally, her curiosity, while endearing, can be dangerous: she’s been known to wander off to follow a rare butterfly or explore a glowing fungus in the midst of a mission, leaving more goal-oriented companions exasperated. Nissa also struggles with the concept of personal property; to her, if something is on the land, it’s part of the land. She doesn’t quite grasp why, for example, picking herbs from a lord’s private garden might anger him. This innocent disregard for man-made rules can land her in hot water, even though her intentions are usually harmless.
char10.ideals: Harmony — Nissa believes in the fundamental balance of nature. Each creature, each plant, has its role in the grand tapestry, and she strives to protect that equilibrium. Civilization and nature can coexist, but only if people remember that they are part of the ecosystem, not its masters. Freedom is also essential to her: the freedom to grow, roam, and be one’s true self, as unconfined as a river or an eagle’s flight. She has little use for man-made laws but an intrinsic obedience to the laws of nature.
char10.name: Nissa
char10.personalityTraits: Nissa is whimsical, curious, and often enchantingly out-of-step with modern life. She tends to tilt her head and listen intently to things others cannot hear—the distant call of an owl at midday or the complaints of an overwatered houseplant—and then acts on that information as though it were common knowledge. She has a habit of giving everyone she meets a nature-inspired nickname ("Sunshine", "Tall-Stag", "Little Acorn") based on what their spirit reminds her of. Nissa’s mood is usually bright and buoyant; she greets each morning with wide-eyed enthusiasm (sometimes literally rising with the sun to watch it, clapping softly at its beauty). Her laughter is a light, trilling sound that often comes at unexpected moments—like in the middle of tense silence, simply because a ladybug landed on someone’s nose. She moves with a kind of flowing, dance-like ease, as if music from the natural world guides her steps (and indeed, she hums melodies she claims the wind taught her). Though gentle, Nissa is not meek. When confronted with deliberate cruelty or devastation of nature, she can become surprisingly stern, even fierce—scolding a lumberjack for cutting a young tree without reason or standing nose-to-chest with a burly bandit to lecture him on compassion (much to his confusion). She’s deeply empathetic; if a companion is hurt or sorrowful, Nissa will be right there, perhaps braiding healing herbs into their hair or producing a small woodland creature to cuddle as comfort. Every so often, especially under a full moon, she grows wistful and dreamy, speaking of ancient forest spirits or wondering aloud what the stars might taste like if you could eat them. In sum, Nissa can be as refreshing—and as unpredictable—as a breeze through the trees: one moment playful and capricious, the next wise and calming, but always utterly true to her nature.

char11.appearance: A lithe wood elf with bark-brown hair in a tight braid and pale green eyes. Weathered cloak, muted leathers, and fletching dyed to match the undergrowth. A single raven feather hangs from the bowstring as a quiet token to fallen friends.
char11.backstory: Talan learned the bow as a forager-turned-scout for a frontier village. When logging crews angered local fey, he negotiated peace by returning a stolen dryad seed. Since then he travels as a mediator between roads and roots, guiding caravans safely while sabotaging those who harm the wilds.
char11.bonds: Protect the border forest; honor the dryad who spared his life; keep a promise to teach a village child archery.
char11.flaws: Distrusts cities; tends to act first if trees are threatened.
char11.ideals: Balance—civilization may pass, the forest endures.
char11.name: Talan
char11.personalityTraits: Soft-spoken, methodical; whistles bird calls instead of shouting.

char12.appearance: An elderly human in simple linens and prayer-worn vestments, silver hair tied back, eyes the calm blue of morning sky. A polished wooden staff doubles as walking stick and holy symbol.
char12.backstory: Sister Amaya served decades as a hospice nurse in a cliffside monastery. When raiders struck coastal hamlets, she left cloistered life to bring field medicine and miracles to the roads, vowing to be the last to leave any battlefield.
char12.bonds: Protect the sick; keep the monastery’s beacon lit each solstice; write letters to the orphan she sponsors.
char12.flaws: Will not abandon a patient, even when retreat is wise.
char12.name: Sister Amaya
char12.personalityTraits: Firm bedside manner, warm humor, unflappable in crisis.

char13.appearance: A bespectacled rock gnome with ink-stained fingers, wild copper hair, and a patchwork robe full of stitched pockets. A tiny clockwork owl perches on the shoulder, ticking softly.
char13.backstory: Pimm was the junior cataloger in a ruined-library dig. A collapsed stack revealed a half-burnt spellbook; restoring it sparked her career. She now hunts lost formulae, trading repairs on village mills for rumors of buried vaults.
char13.bonds: Protect the clockwork owl built with her mentor; finish restoring the burnt grimoire.
char13.flaws: Absentminded; will test wards in unsafe places.
char13.ideals: Knowledge is a commons to be preserved.
char13.name: Pimm Copperleaf

char14.appearance: Tabaxi with dappled snow-leopard fur, bright teal eyes, and silver bells braided into whisker-beads. Wears layered scarves and soft-soled boots; always in motion.
char14.backstory: Skips-of-Stars grew up roof-running above a desert bazaar, lifting purses and stories with equal skill. A traveling pirate told of distant constellations; Skips vowed to see them all. Now a swashbuckler who steals from tyrants and tips tavern staff lavishly.
char14.bonds: Protect street kids; a map of star-inked tattoos guides future journeys.

initiativeBreakdown: Swashbuckler: +4 (Rakish Audacity uses CHA, here +0; use Alert instead)

char14.flaws: Compulsive show-off; risks too much for a flourish.
char14.ideals: Freedom—no cages, not even gilded ones.
char14.name: Skips-of-Stars
char14.personalityTraits: Flirty quips, acrobatic entrances, generous tipper.

char15.appearance: Dragonborn of burnished brass, ritual scars along the jaw, eyes like molten coin. Wears immaculate half-plate etched with legal maxims.
char15.backstory: Once a contract-smith for a mercenary guild, Rhogar turned paladin after witnessing a commander void veterans’ pensions. He swore the Oath of Vengeance to hunt oathbreakers and enforce the spirit of bargains.
char15.bonds: A ledger of broken contracts; a promise to a widow to find her husband’s embezzled pay.
char15.flaws: Rigid about promises; shows little mercy to perjurers.
char15.name: Rhogar Ledgerbane
char15.personalityTraits: Formal speech, relentless focus, surprising dry wit.

char16.appearance: A spare, serene wood elf monk in sand-colored wraps; knuckles scarred, eyes bright as spring leaves. Barefoot, light as thistle-down.
char16.backstory: After years in a cliffside cloister copying sutras, Syllin descended to test compassion against the world’s grit. They break up bar brawls with open-hand grace and deliver rice, not sermons.
char16.bonds: A bell from the cloister; a vow to never strike first in anger.
char16.flaws: Overconfident in de-escalation; will take hits rather than break vow.
char16.name: Syllin
char16.personalityTraits: Dry humor, patient listener, sudden lightning when needed.

char17.appearance: Dwarf with soot-dark beard in copper rings, goggles atop a shaved head, leather apron over breastplate. The iron defender hound at his side hums softly.
char17.backstory: Brunna Ironcoil left the forges to patent an automaton prosthetic for miners. War funding diverted her workshop; now she adventurers to bankroll inventions and field-test prototypes.
char17.bonds: Protect her apprentices; repay a loan to a rival smith—honor demands it.
char17.flaws: Tinkers under pressure; analysis paralysis mid-fight.
char17.ideals: Make better tools; save more lives.
char17.name: Brunna Ironcoil

char18.appearance: Tiefling with violet skin, silver eyes, and curling onyx horns. A lapis lute slung across a brocade vest; smiles like a secret.
char18.backstory: Verity abandoned a noble house to sing truths they would not hear. Her ballads expose corruption, and her illusions keep angry lords guessing. She tours border towns, funding free schools with the takings.
char18.bonds: A promise to a printer who runs a banned press; a list of names to clear in song.
char18.flaws: Compelled to reveal awkward truths; taunts the powerful.
char18.name: Verity Sable

char19.appearance: Half-orc with iron-gray skin and ritual scars across the chest. Wears a bear pelt over spiked armor; eyes like storm-slate.
char19.backstory: Once pit-fighter, now sellsword captain. Drog favors decisive ambushes and leaves warnings carved in stone. He believes fear is cheaper than war.
char19.bonds: His crew; a blood-oath to win a freedman’s rights for orcs in one border city.
char19.name: Drog Stone-Fall

char20.appearance: Firbolg druid with mossy beard beads and tattooed rings like tree growth. Robes woven from nettle-fiber; smells faintly of rain.
char20.backstory: Elm-of-Rain tended a mountain cirque where cloudwater gathers. Miners poisoned the run-off; Elm negotiated remediation with civic mages and, when talks failed, called storms to wash slag pits clean.
char20.bonds: Guard the waters that feed three valleys; a friendly roc nests near his home ridge.
char20.flaws: Slow to trust industry; overuses weather to make a point.
char20.name: Elm-of-Rain
char20.personalityTraits: Gentle cadence, sudden thunder when roused.

char21.appearance: Half-elf in a charcoal frock coat laced with silver sigils, cane-saber at hip, eyes with faint clockwork irises.
char21.backstory: Aramis fled a stifling court to study the Weave’s mechanics. He duels with equations, not blades, and moonlights as a masked “spell duelist” who dismantles enemy magic mid-cast.
char21.bonds: A pact with a street witch who saved him; protect the working mages’ guild.
char21.flaws: Smug about theory; underestimates brute force.
char21.name: Aramis Vale

char22.appearance: Human with smith’s shoulders and callused hands; travels in chain shirt under soot-streaked apron, a war pick slung through a tool belt.
char22.backstory: Mara forged weapons for others until a siege forced her onto the wall. She discovered she prefers swinging what she makes. Now she carries a collapsible spear of her own design and tutors apprentices for free.
char22.bonds: Protect apprentices; donate arms to village watches.
char22.flaws: Workaholic; refuses to abandon a forge under threat.
char22.name: Mara Anvil-by-Dawn
char22.personalityTraits: Gruff mentor energy; belly laugh; exacting safety rules.

char23.appearance: Sea-blue skin, pearly eyes, and hair like dark kelp; bronze scales trace her forearms. A trident-and-storm motif is etched across well-kept scale mail, and seawater beads never seem to cling to her.
char23.backstory: Raised in a reef-sanctum, Thalassa learned to calm storms and succor sailors. After a tyrant navy blockaded trade, she took to the surface to break press-gangs and free conscripts, carrying her god’s thunder into harbor alleys.
char23.bonds: Protect coastal folk; honor the lighthouse keepers that signal safe passage.
char23.flaws: Rushes to punish oath-breakers at sea; distrusts admirals and bureaucrats.
char23.ideals: Freedom travels the trade winds; let no tyrant chain a harbor.
char23.name: Thalassa Tidebound
char23.personalityTraits: Booming laugh, sailor’s sayings, prays before every storm.

char24.appearance: A lithe high elf with inked calligraphy on the forearms, hair bound with silver cords. A slim blade doubles as an arcane focus; robes cut for movement.
char24.backstory: Scholar of war-poetry turned duelist of the Weave, Ilyrion blends dance forms and spellcraft. He left the ivory tower after defending students from a mage-hunter cabal and now teaches ‘bladesong’ to commoners who’ll never see a noble court.
char24.bonds: Protect his students; preserve a lost anthology of battle-odes.
char24.flaws: Overconfident when bladesong is active; disdainful of brute tactics.
char24.ideals: Art in motion—beauty can be a shield for the weak.
char24.name: Ilyrion Valequill

char25.appearance: Square-jawed human in practical chain, shield painted with a chessboard. A travel-stained spellbook hangs from his belt beside a whetstone.
char25.backstory: Veteran of a city watch, Corren studied battlefield cantrips from a hedge mage to even the odds. He now escorts caravans through mage-haunted passes, mixing tactics, steel, and spells.
char25.bonds: Keep trade roads safe; send stipends to the watch widow fund.
char25.flaws: Too cautious; prefers slow, methodical advances.
char25.name: Corren Blackbar
char25.personalityTraits: Dry humor, checks corners, hates surprises.

char26.appearance: A cheerful stout halfling with auburn curls and ink on the fingertips, bandolier of tools and a bright green cloak.
char26.backstory: Pip got bored cracking vaults and now steals secrets instead of coin. She frames corrupt bosses by planting their own ledgers in all the right places.
char26.bonds: Looks after the orphans behind the bakery; owes a retired locksmith her life.
char26.flaws: Compulsively meddles in other people’s locks and secrets.
char26.ideals: Expose the powerful; empower the small.
char26.name: Pip Greenbottle
char26.personalityTraits: Sunny banter, quick hands, quicker exits.

char27.appearance: Towering goliath with granite tattoos, half plate strapped over travel furs; keeps a bundle of practice poles for drills.
char27.backstory: A caravan guard captain who trains village militias on the side. Korr breaks sieges with disciplined shock tactics and a whistle’s code.
char27.bonds: Protects a mountain pass town that fed him during a blizzard.
char27.flaws: Dislikes improvisation; can be overprotective of recruits.
char27.name: Korr Stonewhistle

char28.appearance: Gunmetal warforged with botanical etchings and glass vials nested in the chest cavity; eyes glow soft green.
